back: CNN encodes the image; an RNN decoder emits one word per step with softmax over the vocabulary; trained with cross-entropy.

front: Decoder input at step t in the practical session
back: Concatenation of the previous word embedding and the image feature vector.

front: Why teacher forcing, padding and masking?
back: Train on next-word cross-entropy with the true previous words; pad to batch captions and mask padded positions out of the loss.
Soft: weighted average, differentiable. Hard: pick one region, non-differentiable, trained with REINFORCE.
Avoids squeezing the image into one vector; each word can look at the relevant region.
Sampling draws words at random; beam search keeps the best few partial captions. The deck lists beam search as an improvement.
Clipped unigram precision times brevity penalty $\min(1,e^{1-\rho/|c|})$ with $\rho$ the closest reference length.
So that repeating a matching word ('the the the') cannot inflate precision.
No synonyms, no word order, no check that relations between objects are right.
Input: image and question; output: answer. Needs image model, text model, their interaction and some reasoning.
CNN features of the image and RNN encoding of the question, fused, then a classifier over frequent answers (or a generator).
Priors such as 'tennis' 41% for 'what sport'. VQA 2.0 balances answers across images; VQA-CP shifts priors between train and test.
Always answer the most frequent training answer; a model close to it is not using the image.
